study.question: After replacing example-level positive auxiliary labels by per-task batch means preserved the positive external-orientation advantage, does the orientation bit require task-specific prevalence weights, or does a common pooled auxiliary prevalence suffice?
study.hypothesis: The positive-label-only sign source primarily reflects recipient probability Jacobians rather than task-specific prevalence ratios. Broadcasting the pooled cart/fav/buy batch mean to every auxiliary task should retain the aligned-over-reversed click-AUC gap. This is an unverified local mechanism hypothesis, not a prediction that all auxiliary supervision can be removed.

nearest_work.difference: Direct inherited implementation uses BCE(per-task batch mean)-BCE(0) only for the detached orientation-bit source. Replace per-task means by their common auxiliary average; preserve the true-label objective and native geometry.

Archived primary text lines56-100 describes target-conditioned local activation and weighted history pooling. These are inherited architectural ingredients; this study changes only training-time cotangent source weighting, not the pooling mechanism. No exact paper reproduction or novelty claim.

Pinned benchmark source forward lines123-169 uses task-specific history hubs and stacked interaction before task towers. No such forward exchange is added here; task balance is altered only inside a training-only surrogate sign source. Benchmark code does not verify original-paper equivalence.

Only original-paper link/provenance is available through the registry; detailed text unavailable. Its fallback was read separately. Original-paper mechanism equivalence and broader gradient-method novelty remain unverified.

study.proposed_difference: Add pooled_aux_mean source assignment: mu_pool=mean(y_cart,y_fav,y_buy) over all batch rows and the three auxiliary columns, found by label name. Broadcast this same detached FP32 scalar to every source auxiliary task and row. Contrast with per-task batch means, crossed with external aligned/reversed orientation. Source is sum_aux[BCE(p,mu)-BCE(p,0)] through fixed recipient probabilities; only its detached cotangents select the inherited global orientation bit. Native, cycle, task-mean, pooled-mean and zero source loss graphs execute in all arms. No new feature, parameter, persistent statistic, extra forward, RNG, host optimizer change or inference dependency is introduced.
predictions: The per-task-mean bridge cells reproduce round73 click AUC within absolute1e-6; otherwise implementation/numerical drift blocks interpretation.

With effectively changed source bits and preserved support/norms at a common state, pooled aligned retains most of the per-task aligned advantage over reversed: predicted interaction |(A_pool,+-A_pool,-)-(A_task,+-A_task,-)| <=0.00010 and |A_pool,+-A_task,+| <=0.00010. These are descriptive preregistered practical tolerances, not significance thresholds.

At a fixed state, only the source bit may differ: forward predictions, real scalar BCE, private gradients, native geometry, occupied support and transfer radius remain equal within host FP64/FP32 tolerances. Actual changed context VJP should be a sign flip on the same line when bits disagree.

Expected32192421 parameters and identical inference graph; the extra three pooled BCE nodes increase training graph work equally in all four arms. Host must measure cost rather than infer equal wall time.
falsifiers: A reproducible pooled-vs-task-mean interaction exceeding0.00010 or loss/reversal of the aligned advantage, with effective bit intervention and integrity checks passed, falsifies the proposed task-weight-insensitivity at this configuration. A single-seed result remains preliminary.
A null AUC contrast without fixed-state bit disagreement cannot establish weight irrelevance; it is an ineffective intervention or unresolved probe, not support for the mechanism.

Bridge mismatch >1e-6, changed private gradients, differing support/radius at fixed state, label use in forward, or any frozen-contract violation invalidates attribution and requires correction with all failed costs retained.
No advantage over click-only in future paired-seed full-protocol repeats would falsify a useful transfer benefit. This round alone does not repeat or replace that broader comparison.

Pooled scalar still contains aggregate auxiliary prevalence, and recipient Jacobians retain learned task information
One seed; deterministic replays verify implementation but do not estimate initialization uncertainty
BF16/FP32 BCE saturation, cancellation, task-gradient imbalance and pivot sensitivity can mediate effects
Shared row-space VJP constraints precede repeated-ID scatter; no claim of parameter-space gradient orthogonality

In unsaturated exact BCE arithmetic the positive-label difference has logit derivative -mu, so a common positive pooled scalar can cancel from a scale-invariant bit; residual batch-count information, zero-positive batches and finite precision remain. Similar AUC cannot show no auxiliary information anywhere.
Validation-selected long trajectories and many same-seed comparisons invite selection optimism. Neither the incumbent nor a proposed improvement has authorized withheld confirmation.
External orientation can act as generic optimization bias; the inherited canonical-bit removal and click-bit trajectories are distinct controls, while these four cells isolate task weighting only.
